text.p: British retailer Storehouse Plc on Thursday said it hoped to reverse a two percent decline in like for like sales at its childrens wear chain Mothercare by the end of its current financial year.
Chief executive Keith Edelman said "We'd hope by the year end we would not be in like for like decline."
Edelman told Reuters in a telephone interview Mothercare had not been having such a good time on the sales front because of a difficult childrenswear market.
"I think we've got some work to do at Mothercare... and that's what we're focusing on now."
He said management had been strengthened, splitting responsibilities for clothing and hardwear.

Corporate affairs director Richard Dixon said the chain had been recovering from the final quarter of last year when its performance had deteriorated. Dixon said the group was also introducing new ranges and believed that stock coming in after Christmas this year would be stronger last year's ranges.

Storehouse estimated it has 15 percent of the 0 to 7 year old childrens wear market. "As a group we don't think we've lost market share. We believe that Mothercare has probably lost a bit and Bhs has gained a bit," Edelman said.

Like-for-like sales at Bhs, which excludes new space, were up about three percent, Edelman said. Overall sales at Bhs rose nine percent, of which four percent came from new stores and a further two percent from franchises overseas.
Gross margins across the group were down by about half a percentage point, including Childrens World, which Storehouse bought from Boots Co Plc.
But Dixon said excluding Childrens World and overseas franchises -- which have lower margins -- UK gross margins both in Mothercare and Bhs were up.
Costs rose four percent in the core businesses during the half year, but by 10 percent if Childrens World is included.

Storehouse has converted four Childrens World's 57 out of town sites into Mothercare World and these are generating much higher gross margins, Edelman said. It will convert more after Christmas and over time the Childrens World name will disappear. Storehouse bought the business from Boots for 62.5 million stg.

Overseas, the group expects to have 200 franchises for Bhs and Mothercare by the year end. In Britain, four new Bhs stores are planned to open before the end of March making 140 in total. A further five or six are planned for 1997/98.
